extensions.platform: android (Jetpack Compose, Material 3); dp and sp units; tokens live in ui/theme/*.kt

display-large.purpose: The display serif figure inside the lit hero panel; steps down a rung as the text grows, font scale capped at 1.3x.

display-medium.purpose: The hero figure when its text runs long.

headline-large.purpose: Every screen's serif title, with its sans context line under it.

headline-medium.purpose: A secondary figure inside a panel, such as the net across accounts.

headline-small.purpose: The serif value in a stat tile, over its mono label.

title-small.purpose: The sans header over a slab group, and compact readings.

body-large.purpose: Row titles, field text, segment labels, the context line under a page title.

body-medium.purpose: Row subtitles and the line under a hero figure; the italic aside.

body-small.purpose: Chip text, captions, tile details, legend and nav labels.

label-large.purpose: Mono uppercase panel names, lowercase text actions, a field's currency suffix.

label-medium.purpose: Mono uppercase stat-tile labels under their values, panel readings, day initials.

label-small.purpose: Chart axis ends and the heat grid's day numbers.

mono-action.purpose: The bold mono label on hero and secondary actions, sentence case.

shadows.name: fab-lift
shadows.purpose: The add FAB only; every other surface the app draws is flat and rises by the tonal ladder (the snackbar keeps Material's own 6dp shadow).

surfaces.name: panel-edge
surfaces.purpose: The quiet edge of panels, stat tiles and the nav bar's top.

surfaces.name: hero-light
surfaces.value: linear-gradient(180deg, accent 22%, accent 6%, container) over container; 1dp accent edge at 28%
surfaces.purpose: The one lit hero panel per view.

surfaces.name: glyph-wash
surfaces.purpose: The tinted tile behind every leading glyph.

surfaces.name: selection
surfaces.value: 1dp accent ring (1.5dp on segment thumbs) over a 15% accent wash; idle ring outline at 35%

surfaces.name: muted-floor
surfaces.purpose: The lowest alpha muted text may take and still clear 4.5:1.

surfaces.name: focus-ring
surfaces.value: 2dp stroke in the accent along the target's own shape (12dp corners by default), on its inner edge; the on-accent colour on the hero action; 4dp outside a bare row inside a panel (the Categories and Accounts lists still draw it inside)
surfaces.purpose: Keyboard, D-pad and Chromebook focus only; touch never shows it.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Selection ring and wash, nav pill, tab cross-fade.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: Default enter, exit and state transitions.

motion.name: emphasized
motion.purpose: Pushed screens sliding in by an eighth of the width.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: Meter, bar and chart fills drawing in once.

motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: Fills drawing in: moves at once, settles softly.

motion.name: press-bounce
motion.value: scale 0.97, spring damping medium-bouncy, stiffness medium-low
motion.purpose: The one press language; no ripple except under TalkBack.

motion.name: snappy
motion.purpose: The segmented thumb gliding to its pick.

motion.name: remove-animations
motion.value: animator scale 0 collapses every spec to a cut

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Bottom bar (72dp) and a floating add FAB at bottom end.

breakpoints.name: medium
breakpoints.purpose: An 88dp nav rail at the start with the FAB at its top; Home's column caps at READING_WIDTH (640dp, gutters included) and centres; every other screen stays one full-width column.

breakpoints.name: expanded
breakpoints.purpose: Home splits into two panes under one title: hero, In and Out, week at the start; envelopes, recent, bills, accounts at the end.

breakpoints.name: font-1.3x
breakpoints.purpose: Segments wrap into chips, choice rows and figure rows stack, paired actions stack; hero figure stops growing; Settings tile pairs stack.

breakpoints.name: font-1.5x
breakpoints.purpose: Pairs of stat tiles stack into one column.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Lit Ledger"**

Tally is a month kept as a ledger on a warm near-black desk, with one lamp over the figure that matters. The world is inherited from the sibling app Avex (warm Pearl ground, serif figures, sans rows, mono uppercase labels, one owner-chosen accent) and deliberately made richer at the owner's binding call: every section sits on its own raised panel, every section header and every stat is led by a drawn glyph on a tinted tile, the reading a screen exists for sits in the one accent-lit hero panel, and screens carry more readings and charts than Avex's open page. The result is dense but ordered: blocks of readings, each one quietly edged, none shouting.

Depth is tonal, not cast. Panels are a warm rung above the ground with a 1dp edge; tappable things are a further rung up and edgeless; the hero is lit from its top edge by a wash of the accent. Colour is spent with intent: the accent marks what the owner acts on and where the month stands, the twelve category hues are a data series, and red and green appear only when something is really over or under. Readings travel with their numbers: a meter always carries its pace tick, a figure always carries the line that explains it.

Motion is short and physical. Fills draw in once over 900ms and never replay when a row scrolls back, a press is a 0.97 bounce rather than a ripple, and every animation collapses to a cut when the system's Remove animations is on.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black Pearl ground with a top-to-bottom gradient; a pure-black variant for OLED.
Three type voices: serif figures and titles, sans rows and prose, mono uppercase labels.
One owner-chosen accent (Ember by default), with a near-white fallback when colour is off.
Raised 20dp panels with a 1dp quiet edge, one 24dp lit hero panel per view.
A glyph tile leads every panel header, stat tile and list row.
The pace tick: every meter shows where an even spend would be today.
No dividers anywhere; air and panel edges separate sections.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: The accent is the owner's single colour and the only light in the room. It marks what can be acted on and where the month stands; the hero panel's wash is the only gradient on any raised surface. The ground's own dark fall carries no colour, and the month line's area fade is a data mark, not a light.

rules.name: The Data Series Rule
rules.body: Category hues are data, not decoration: they appear on a category's badge and in charts, never on text, never on chrome. Their order is stored, so a new hue is appended, never inserted or reordered.

rules.name: The True State Rule
rules.body: Red means over, green means in or under, and nothing else wears them. A state colour is a mark, never a paragraph.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Text clears 4.5:1 and marks clear 3:1 on the surface they sit on, and content on an accent fill is chosen by measuring both ends of the palette against it, never by guess. The build's contrast test holds every accent, both grounds and the accent-off fallback to this.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif for THE figure or title of a block, sans for rows and prose, mono for labels and text actions. Sizes come only from the type scale; a call site never sets its own size, and the build fails if one does.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every serif and title style carries tabular digits, so a changing amount never shifts its neighbours.

rules.name: The Context Below Rule
rules.body: A page title stands alone at the top of its column with its context line under it in sans, joined with " · " (for example "18 days left · resets 1 Nov"). Nothing sits above a title.

rules.name: The Serif Is A Role Rule
rules.body: The serif voice is fixed by role and size, not by face. It resolves to the platform serif because the pinned reference, Avex, resolves to exactly that face and the two apps are meant to sit side by side on one phone. If the owner ever unpins Avex, a bundled serif replaces it without changing any size, weight or role here.

rules.name: The Air Not Rules Rule
rules.body: Sections are separated by space and by panel edges, never by a divider or a hairline rule. The build fails on any divider.

rules.name: The Start And End Rule
rules.body: Padding, alignment and chart direction are written in start and end so the whole app mirrors for right-to-left; left and right never appear.

rules.name: The Tonal Ladder Rule
rules.body: A surface rises by stepping up the warm container ladder and taking a 1dp edge, never by casting a shadow. Only the FAB floats.

rules.name: The One Lit Panel Rule
rules.body: A view has exactly one hero panel, for the figure it exists to show. Its tint follows the reading: the accent normally, the over-budget red when the month or budget is over.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Members of a group, keypad keys included, are separated by a 2dp gap of ground, never a line; the group's outer corners are 16dp and its inner corners 4dp.

rules.name: The Glyph Leads Rule
rules.body: Every panel header, stat tile and list row begins with a drawn glyph on its own tinted tile, all from one rounded icon library at one stroke, and no two icon keys share a glyph.

rules.name: The Slab Is A Tap Rule
rules.body: An edgeless container-high slab is always something you press. A panel or stat tile is a section of readings and is not itself a target, the monthly budget's hero being the single exception, because it opens its own editor.

rules.name: The Pace Tick Rule
rules.body: A meter without its pace tick is only half a reading. Wherever an even spend has a meaning, the tick is drawn.

rules.name: The Bounce Rule
rules.body: A press is a 0.97 bounce and a fill is drawn once; when the system's animation scale is zero, every spec collapses to a cut.

dos: Do put every section on one panel (20dp corners, container fill, 1dp outline-variant edge, 18dp padding) with 14dp between panels and a 24dp gutter.
Do lead every panel header and stat tile with a glyph tile (32dp or 30dp, 10dp corners, the accent on a 16% wash) and every row with a glyph badge (44dp, 36dp on a denser row inside a panel).
Do give each view exactly one hero panel for its main figure, tinted red when that figure is over.
Do draw the pace tick on every meter where an even spend means something, and let an overrun show as a red length past a budget notch.
Do take every colour from the scheme or the category palette and every size from the type scale.
Do set titles and figures in serif, rows in sans, labels in spaced mono capitals, and join readings with " · ".
Do hold text to 4.5:1 and marks to 3:1 on the surface they sit on, and keep muted text at 0.65 alpha or more.
Do let every row and control grow with its text at 200% and let readings drop under their labels rather than break; a panel header's label keeps one line.
Do match a screen to its window: from 600dp cap a single column at READING_WIDTH (640dp) and centre it, as Home does, and from 840dp give Home its two panes.
Do write layout in start and end, and draw charts from the reading edge in right-to-left.
Do make a press a 0.97 bounce and make every animation collapse to a cut when animations are removed.
Do draw keyboard and D-pad focus as a 2dp accent ring along the target's own shape, and announce a one-of-many choice as a radio button in a selectable group.
donts: Don't draw a divider or hairline rule between sections; space and panel edges do that work.
Don't use a Material top app bar or name the screen in the top bar; the serif page title names it.
Don't put a label above a page title or a heading; context goes under it.
Don't set a font size or a raw colour at a call site.
Don't nest a panel inside a panel, or box the interactive rows inside a panel.
Don't put a category hue on text or chrome, or reorder the hues.
Don't use red or green for anything but a true over, under or money-in state, and never for body text.
Don't cast shadows from panels, tiles or slabs; only the FAB lifts.
Don't wash the accent over sheets and menus; tonal depth is the warm ladder.
Don't cut user content to one line.
Don't use left or right in layout.
